36 In deriving a formula for the combined resistance of three different resistors in series, Kirchhoff’s
laws are used.
Which physics principle is involved in this derivation?
A
the conservation of charge
B
the direction of the flow of charge is from negative to positive
C
the potential difference across each resistor is the same
D
the current varies in each resistor, in proportion to the resistor value

hints: Notice the words three resistors in series - there is only one conducting loop with no junctions between the resistors.
Recall what Kirchhoff's first law says about current at a junction with no storage of charge, and apply it where the wire joins one series resistor to the next.
Compare series with parallel: decide which quantity must stay the same through each resistor and which quantity adds up to give $R = R_1 + R_2 + R_3$.
walkthrough: Identify the circuit: three different resistors in series form a single loop, so charge flowing out of one resistor flows directly into the next with nowhere else to go.
State the physical rule: Kirchhoff's first law is conservation of charge, $\sum I_{in} = \sum I_{out}$, so no net charge builds up at the connections.
Apply it to series: with no branches, the current $I$ must be identical in resistor 1, resistor 2 and resistor 3.
Complete the derivation logic: Kirchhoff's second law then gives $V = V_1 + V_2 + V_3$, and with $V = IR$ this becomes $IR = IR_1 + IR_2 + IR_3$.
Cancel the common $I$ to get $R = R_1 + R_2 + R_3$, which was only possible because conservation of charge made $I$ the same. This is option A.

A.explanation: In series there is one path, so charge cannot accumulate and the current $I$ is the same in all three resistors - this is Kirchhoff's first law, conservation of charge.

B.explanation: The derivation uses magnitudes of current and potential difference, not whether electron flow is negative to positive or conventional current is positive to negative.

C.explanation: Equal potential difference across each resistor applies to parallel, not series - in series the total $V = V_1 + V_2 + V_3$.

D.explanation: In series the current does not split, so it is the same in each resistor and the larger resistor gets the larger share of potential difference.
